definitions.explanation: A form of traditional Japanese comic theater performed between noh plays, featuring humorous everyday situations.
A made-up story or false claim, especially one used to deceive.

examples.japanese: {能|のう}と{狂言|きょうげん}を{観|み}た。
{狂言|きょうげん}は{滑稽|こっけい}な{話|はなし}が{多|おお}い。
これは{狂言|きょうげん}{強盗|ごうとう}だ。

notes:
COMPOUND: {狂|きょう} (crazy, wild) + {言|げん} (words)

TRADITIONAL THEATER:
Kyogen is performed as comic relief between serious noh plays. Unlike noh's supernatural themes, kyogen features everyday characters in humorous situations.

CHARACTERISTICS:
・Spoken dialogue (not chanted like noh)
・Simple costumes and no masks (usually)
・Common character types: clever servants (太郎冠者), foolish masters

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{狂言|きょうげん}を{演|えん}じる (to perform kyogen)
・{狂言|きょうげん}{師|し} (kyogen actor)
・{狂言|きょうげん}{回|まわ}し (comic interlude narrator)

SENSE 2 (MODERN USAGE):
・{狂言|きょうげん}{強盗|ごうとう} (fake robbery)
・{狂言|きょうげん}{誘拐|ゆうかい} (fake kidnapping)
